LanguageData.RatkinQL_Legendary_NamedText:
The client takes the {2} {1} and turns it over for a long while, then raps the flat of it once with a knuckle.

"A weapon like this should not go without a name."

They name it there in front of you. From today it is called "{0}".

You have no idea where it will end up, or in whose hands. But this is how smithing works: the piece leaves your door, and only then does your name start travelling. If word ever comes back, it will most likely be about this one.
LanguageData.RatkinQL_Legendary_Tale1:
A ratkin pedlar stands at your smithy for a long time before speaking. "That {1} they call '{0}'... I saw it at the southern market. Slung across the back of a one-eyed veteran. He would not sell it at any price."

The old soldier had said only one thing, apparently: it stopped a blow for him once, and he does not intend to let it off his back again.

(That was your work, {3} days ago. Your name is travelling with it.)
LanguageData.RatkinQL_Legendary_Tale2:
The news from the border is not good: "{0}" was taken in an ambush.

The whole caravan was carried off, and nobody can say who holds that {2} {1} now. Some say it went into a warlord's armoury. Others say it was broken down and sold for materials.

(It was good work. But a smith does not get to decide where the work ends up. When you handed it over {3} days ago, this was not the ending you pictured.)
LanguageData.RatkinQL_Legendary_Tale3:
Someone has put "{0}" into a song.

A ratkin storyteller working the taverns passes through and performs a piece about a border garrison - and the {1} in it, the one that made an enemy line step back the moment it was drawn, carries a name you recognise. He has no idea the smith who made it is sitting in the audience.

({3} days, from a bar of stock to a verse in a song. Sometimes this is how the trade pays you.)
LanguageData.RatkinQL_Legendary_Tale4:
An unsigned note, the letters pressed hard into the paper:

"'{0}' is still with us. Three people have carried it and all three came home. The fourth asked me to pass this on to whoever forged it - thank you."

Underneath the note is a small weight of silver, sent back in thanks.

(You handed over that {2} {1} {3} days ago. At the time it was just another order.)
